title: Pay insurance duty on premiums (insurers)
what: An insurer pays duty on the premiums for the insurance it writes in the state, and usually passes it on to the insured.

sources.title: Duties Act 2001 (Qld)
sources.quote: 357 Who is liable to pay insurance duty (1) Insurance duty imposed on general insurance must be paid by the insurer. (2) Insurance duty imposed on life insurance must be paid by the insurer.

administration.who: Queensland Revenue Office (Commissioner of State Revenue)

sources.title: Duties Act 2001 (Qld)
sources.locator: sch 6, def commissioner, words naming the body (found 18 Nov 2026) (current)
sources.quote: commissioner means the Commissioner of State Revenue appointed under the Administration Act .

sources.title: Duties Act 2001 (Qld)
sources.quote: 357 Who is liable to pay insurance duty (1) Insurance duty imposed on general insurance must be paid by the insurer. (2) Insurance duty imposed on life insurance must be paid by the insurer.

confidence_note: The Act's own words make the insurer liable for the duty (in the NT, the quote is the duty to register as an insurer before writing dutiable policies).

assessment.summary: A tax on insurance premiums on top of GST. It discourages people and businesses from insuring and leaves more risk unpooled; the Henry Review recommended abolishing all such taxes.

marks.reason: Raises the price of insurance relative to other services, so people under-insure (Henry Review).

assessment.confidence_note: The direction is well supported; no official estimate of the efficiency cost of insurance duty was found. Marks copied from the register item qld-insurance-duty so the two agree.
